ideas.hypothesis: Situational (Delaware-style, conflict-specific) independence of directors predicts lower fraud incidence better than SOX-style outsider-status independence, especially when directors receive valuation-model-level information.

sources.role: mechanism/measure: contrast between SOX outsider-status and Delaware situational independence
setting: Enron agency failures that SOX did not address
mechanism: directors need detailed information (DCF models) to monitor

ideas.test: US firms 2003-2019; code social/professional ties of directors to the CEO (situational independence) alongside formal independence; logit of AAER/SEC enforcement or securities class action incidence on both measures, controlling for size and industry.
ideas.disconfirming: Situational independence has no incremental predictive power for fraud beyond formal independence.

ideas.hypothesis: After a negative growth shock, firms with high managerial ownership and weak internal governance shift payout toward dividends rather than repurchases and are more likely to undertake diversifying acquisitions, while strong external governance offsets this.

sources.role: finding/method: exogenous growth shock and payout response by internal/external governance
mechanism: managerial risk exposure leads to diversifying acquisitions after liability shocks
measure: insider ownership as moderator of board quality effects

ideas.test: Use an exogenous industry demand shock (e.g. tariff or regulatory shock) in Compustat/ExecuComp firms; difference-in-differences of payout mix and acquisition activity by terciles of managerial ownership and an internal-governance index.
ideas.disconfirming: Payout mix and acquisition responses to the shock do not differ by managerial ownership or internal governance.

ideas.hypothesis: Independent directors with high network centrality (many interlocks) substitute for a weak market for corporate control: in settings with few hostile bids, central independent directors are associated with stronger CEO turnover-performance sensitivity.

sources.role: measure: centrality and density as board power
setting: underdeveloped German market for corporate control and interlocks
mechanism: takeover defenses limit market for control
finding: independent commissioners moderate performance relations

ideas.test: Panel of German and UK listed firms 2000-2019 with BoardEx interlocks; logit of CEO turnover on performance interacted with independent-director centrality and a country/firm takeover-exposure measure.
ideas.disconfirming: Centrality effects on turnover sensitivity are no larger where takeover pressure is weak.

ideas.hypothesis: CEO duality raises the probability of compensation-related scandals only when the compensation committee lacks fully independent members; with independent compensation committees duality has no effect.

sources.role: finding: review of independent directors, duality and committees
mechanism: compensation committee practices to avoid scandal
mechanism: board information deficits in scandals
method: interaction-effect regression

ideas.test: US firms 2000-2019 from ExecuComp/BoardEx; dependent variable is backdating, compensation-related lawsuits or say-on-pay failure; logit with duality x compensation-committee independence interaction.
ideas.disconfirming: Duality increases scandal risk equally regardless of committee independence, or not at all.

ideas.hypothesis: In Chinese listed companies, audit committee financial expertise improves earnings quality only where the largest shareholder's coalition of related shareholders is balanced by other active blockholders.

sources.role: finding/measure: shareholder relationships and active ownership improve earnings quality
measure: audit committee independence and financial expertise
setting: Chinese governance reform and board characteristics
finding: audit committee structure may lack effect on returns

ideas.test: CSMAR data on A-share firms 2010-2019: discretionary accruals regressed on audit committee expertise, active-shareholder balance measure and their interaction.
ideas.disconfirming: Audit committee expertise improves earnings quality equally regardless of shareholder balance, or not at all.

ideas.hypothesis: Reforms mandating independent directors reduce financial distress risk more in firms with low managerial ownership, because high managerial ownership already aligns incentives (substitute mechanisms).

sources.role: setting: worldwide reforms on independent directors
measure/finding: governance characteristics and financial distress in Indonesia
mechanism: insider ownership moderates board effects

ideas.test: Difference-in-differences around an emerging-market independent-director mandate (e.g. Indonesia or India Clause 49); distress probability by pre-reform managerial ownership.
ideas.disconfirming: The reform's effect on distress is equal or larger in high-managerial-ownership firms.

ideas.hypothesis: Independent boards act more as mediating hierarchs than as shareholder agents: higher board independence is associated with lower payout to shareholders and higher stakeholder-specific investment (R&D, employee training) in firms with high growth opportunities.

sources.role: mechanism: team production model with board as mediator vs shareholder primacy
measure: definitions of independence
finding: independent commissioners moderate IOS-performance relation
setting: law and governance debates on stakeholders

ideas.test: US panel 2000-2019; regress payout ratio and R&D/employee investment on board independence, using exchange independence mandates of 2002-2003 as instrument.
ideas.disconfirming: Higher independence increases payout and reduces stakeholder investment.

ideas.hypothesis: In family-controlled firms, CEO duality increases (rather than decreases) CEO turnover-performance sensitivity, because controlling shareholders use the combined role to hold the CEO directly accountable, consistent with controlling-shareholder primacy.

sources.role: finding: turnover-performance sensitivity higher with duality in Thailand
mechanism: shareholder primacy vs team production
method: interaction regressions
setting: governance norm debate

ideas.test: Thai and Indonesian listed firms 2005-2019; logit of CEO turnover on ROA x duality x family control.
ideas.disconfirming: Duality reduces turnover sensitivity in family firms.

ideas.hypothesis: Independent-director reforms are less effective in improving performance in firms with high ownership concentration, because blockholders choose nominally independent directors loyal to them.

sources.role: finding: independent directors often contribute little despite reforms
measure: external blockholders and independent commissioners

ideas.test: Event-study/DiD of Tobin's Q around an independent-director mandate in an emerging market, split by largest-shareholder stake.
ideas.disconfirming: Reform effects are equal or larger in highly concentrated firms.

ideas.hypothesis: Demographic and functional diversity of the audit committee strengthens the governance-risk relationship: diverse audit committees are associated with lower financial risk-taking than homogeneous ones of equal independence.

sources.role: finding/method: committee-level governance and risk via PLS-SEM in India
mechanism: social categorization perspective on boards
setting: committee structures
finding: audit committee structure may not affect returns

ideas.test: NSE-listed Indian firms 2014-2019; regress stock return volatility and leverage on audit committee diversity index (gender, expertise, age), controlling for independence.
ideas.disconfirming: Audit committee diversity has no relation or a positive relation with risk-taking.
